MRI enhanced with MMCM is capable of characterizing tumors for prognosis, treatment, and monitoring therapeutic response.
MRI assays of tumor angiogenesis can be used for prognostication and to monitor the response of tumors to anti-angiogenic therapy.
MRI enhanced with MMCM can be applied to assay tumor microvasculature and can be used to monitor therapeutic response.

the application of macromolecular contrast agents for the non-invasive detection and characterization of tumors and their angiogenesis.
developing MRI methods that will provide a means for non-invasive, in vivo characterization of tumors, and for monitoring changes in tumor characteristics in response to therapeutic interventions.
development of a novel MRI method for the non-invasive assessment of tumor angiogenesis.

MRI with macromolecular contrast agents has the potential to be a powerful and versatile clinical tool for the assessment of tumor angiogenesis and for the non-invasive monitoring of therapeutic responses.

MMCM-enhanced dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI provides a means to characterize tumors noninvasively and to monitor changes in microvessels that result from administration and/or inhibition of angiogenic factors, thereby providing a means to optimize treatment of cancer.
MMCM-enhanced MR imaging has great promise for the noninvasive evaluation of angiogenesis and for monitoring the response to therapy.

the macromolecular contrast agent, which has the ability to extravasate from the blood into the tumor interstitial space, can be used to assess tumor microvessels.

the MRI characterization of tumors with a macromolecule contrast medium (MMCC) is a promising technique that may provide a means to assess tumor microvascular characteristics noninvasively and in real time.

the use of macromolecular contrast agents in the clinical setting will provide a means to characterize tumors for prognoses, individualize treatment and monitor therapeutic response, and that this technology can be applied in a clinical setting.
